caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 934 of 2008
lawyer:
MI Farooqui, Senior Advocate instructed by MG Bhuiyan, Advocate-on-Record----- For the Petitioner. 
Not Represented----- For the Respondents.
parties:
Syed Afsaruddin ----- Petitioner 
Vs.
Bangladesh and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
2. In the writ petition the listing of the case property as an abandoned property has been challenged by the writ petitioner claiming to be the purchaser-owner of the case property on the basis of an agreement for sale dated 21-1-1972 with the original lessee of the case property and that the writ petitioner got the required sale deed executed and registered through Court by filling Title Suit No.121 of1981 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka, for Specific Performance of Contract as the original lessee id not execute and register the required sale deed inspite of receiving of Taka 11,000 against the consideration amount fixed' at Taka 15,000 on three different occasions and that the writ petitioner got delivery of possession of the case property on 26-1-1984 through Court and that the Government, a defendant in the aforesaid Title Suit No.121 of 1981, through filed an application for restoration of the case under Order 9 RuIe 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure, registered as Miscellaneous Case No. 218 of 1986, and the same was dismissed for default on 18-3-1990 and that the suit property has been enlisted in the 'Ka' list of the abandoned properties published in the gazette dated 23-9-1986 and that the writ petitioner moved the Settlement Court under the provisions of the Abandoned Property Buildings (Supplementary Provisions) Ordinance, 1985 (Ordinance 54/85) for release of the property from the list of abandoned properties being Case No. 106 of 1995. 

 3. The government contested the case, asserting, that the original lessee being a non-Bengali left the country in 1971, his whereabouts could not be known after the liberation of Bangladesh on 16-12-1971 and that the government has been in physical possession and management of the case holding since 1972 and enlisted the same as abandoned property and allowed Syed Aftab Uddin, a Demand Note holder as licensee under the Government to and occupy the case holding. The Court of Settlement on perusal of the Government file and on consideration of the materials on record submitted by the writ petitioner rejected the prayer for release by the impugned judgment and order dated 7-9-1997 and hence the writ petition. 

 4. The High Court Division discharged the Rule observing that in view of the decision of the Appellate Division in the case of Rawshan Ara Begum vs Bangladesh reported in 59 DLR (AD) 165, wherein it has been held that the listing of the property as an abandoned property even without service of notice as per provision of Ordinance No. 54 of1985 will be lawful and that decree through which the writ petitioner alleged to have got the sale deed executed and registered as well as the possession of the case property through Court, is on the basis of a decree passed for Specific Performance of Contract and not for declaration that the suit property is not an abandoned property and, as such, the said decree cannot be set up as a bar against inclusion of the case property in the list of abandoned property which is supported by the decisions in the case of CQMH Md Ayub Ali vs Bangladesh reported in 47 DLR (AD) 71 as well as in the case of Bangladesh vs Md Shahjahan reported in 5 MLR (AD) 237 = 5 BLC (AD) 25. The High Court Division also relied on a decision of the Appellate Division in the case of Bangladesh vs Md Suruzzamal reported in 15 BLD (AD) 146 = 48 DLR (AD) 1, wherein their lordships held that once a property vests in the Government under PO No. 16 of 1972 no legal proceedings can be brought against such property. The High Court Division in the instant case, referring to the decision of the Settlement Court, has observed that: 

 "In the instant case the Settlement Court opined that the Government included the suit property in the abandoned property list after observing all the formalities of law and where- about of the original lessee Md Moslem was not known but the petitioner could not produce any evidence or documents that the original lessee Mr Moslem was very much present in Bangladesh before or after the promulgation of PO 16 of 1972. In this context the Settlement Court discussed the evidence of the son of said Muslim and also perused the documents filed by the petitioner and the Government and opined that the petitioner could not prove that the original lessee was very much present in Bangladesh or he has ceased to occupy or man- age or supervise or control the property when the PO 16 of 1972 came into force. In such a situation the High Court Division cannot up set the such findings of facts under its extra-ordinary jurisdiction under Article 102 of the Constitution. In the case of Government of Bangladesh represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Works vs Jalil reported in 49 DLR (AD) 26, 48 DLR (AD) 10, 15 BLD (AD) 175 wherein their lordship held that the High Court Division exercising power under Article 102 of the Constitution does not work as a Court of appeal and, as such, it is not required to make determination offacts of its own. It can interfere with the findings of a Tribunal of facts under its extra ordinary jurisdiction under Article 102 only if it can be shown that the Tribunal has without jurisdiction or made any finding upon no evidence or without considering any material evidence/facts causing prejudice to the complaining party or it has acted malafide or in violation of the principle of natural justice in the absence of any such conditions the interference by the High Court Division itself becomes an act without jurisdiction and in the present case this precisely has happened. It has been further held that the onus, lies on the claimant of the building to prove that the building is not abandoned property. The Government has no obligation either to deny the facts alleged by the claimant or to disclose the basis of treating the property as abandoned property. 

 Similar view has been taken in the case of Government of Bangladesh vs Ashraf Ali @ Ashraf Ali and another reported in 49 DLR (AD) 161 wherein it has been held that no rebuttable evidence could be adduced to show that original owner Yahiya was present in Bangladesh and he occupied, managed or supervised the disputed building when President's Order 16 of 1972 came into operation." 

 5. We have perused the leave petition and considered the submissions of the learned Advocate appearing for the leave petitioner and the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division. The learned Advocate appearing for the leave petitioner persuaded us on the ground that before enlistment of the property in the list of abandoned properties, no notice as required under the provision of Article 5 of the Ordinance 54 of 1985, was issued and thereby the impugned enlistment of the case property is without lawful authority. It appears from the record that the writ petitioner has claimed his possession in the case property since 21-1-1972, the alleged date of his agreement for sale of the case property with the original lessee under the Government. It is also stated by the writ petitioner that he got possession of the case property through Court by filing Execution Case, after getting a decree in is suit for Specific Performance of Contract relating to the agreement dated 20-1-1972 and the said suit was decreed ex-parte on 1-6-1986 and the required sale deed was executed on 15-12-1983 and delivery of possession was received by the writ petitioner on 26-1-1984 through Title Execution Case No.38 of 1983 and it is also on record that the Government has issued demand note for payment of rent on the prayer of one Syed Aflab Uddin, who was in possession of the case property, and in view of the issuance of such demand note, the possession of the Government on the case holding trough the Demand Note holder is ex-facie proved and the delivery of possession as claimed by the. writ petitioner through Court also proved the claim of the writ petitioner's on the suit property since 20-1-1971 as false and thus the enlistment of the case property as an abandoned property cannot be said to be not in accordance with law inasmuch as the Government's possession in the case property has been proved. It further appeared from the tax payment receipts of the Dhaka Municipal Corporation, annexed to the writ petition as Annexure-J and J(1), and the electricity bills, annexed as Annexures-J-2 and J-3, that till 1987 one Mrs Aktary Begum was in possession on the case property and said Mrs Aktary Begum also was made a party in the Title Suit No.1211 of 1981 filed by the writ petitioner for Specific performance of Contract in respect of the case property, which also goes against the claim of the writ petitioner as to his valid ownership and possession in the case property in that the filing of the case for Specific Performance of Contract in respect of the case holding, in view of Article 14 of PO 16 of 1972, is barred and void. 

 6. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case. we are of the view that the enlistment of the case property in the impugned list or abandoned property, as held by the High Court Division in the impugned judgment and order  is in accordance with law and thus there is no merit in the leave petition.
